sentences.text:
Bench: Dipankar Datta, Prashant Kumar Mishra
 In The Supreme Court Of India

CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. OF 2024  (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.13849/2024)
 SAVITA SINGH APPELLANT  VERSUS  THE STATE OF JHARKHAND & ORS. RESPONDENTS  ORDER Leave granted.

2. The High Court by the impugned judgment and order dated 13 th May, 2024 has quashed the relevant FIR under sections 494, 323,341,498A and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 18601 on the ground that the same was the second FIR in the series of FIRs filed by the complainant/respondent without any change of facts or new foundation and that the first FIR did not end in a charge-sheet.

3. Having heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the materials on record,
we are of the considered opinion that the High Court reached a wrong conclusion.
The offence under section 494, IPC was not alleged in the earlier FIR.
The High Court was, therefore, in error in quashing the second FIR.
4. The impugned judgment and order dated 13 th May, 2024 is set aside.
The trial court shall now proceed in accordance with law.
Parties are left free to urge all points that are available to them in law.

Reason:
1 IPC 5.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in the aforesaid terms.
6. Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed.
